finding.text: `Session.turn_title` (public/framework/core/Session/Session.js, the `turn_title` line in the diff) uses `/s+/g` where `/\s+/g` was meant. It replaces every run of the letter "s" with a space, so "Make it blue, please" becomes the title "Make it blue, plea e". No test checks the title, so the tests pass anyway.

Replaying old sessions changes their scores. `apply_line` now turns every historical `{refined:{re,…}}` line into an open Prompt task: about 170 such lines across 19 browser-voice sessions (for example `sessions/2026/10/25/v-sq8y7db/session.jsonl` has 62). Each of those past sessions now drops below 1 in `completion_score()`, and nobody will ever close those tasks. The brief says "Old lines … still replay and render; history is not migrated", which means old lines should replay as they did before. Gate the derivation on lines written from now on (for example `by:"code"`, or a date) or log a decision for it.

The owner's decisions were changed without a logged reason. The task log's only `decision` line is the abandoned `{ask:{…}}` design (commit 852954149). plan.md says "The owner's direction (relayed 21:50) replaced the `{ask}` line", but there is no `decision` line saying so and no link to the owner's words. The new design also stores the words twice on every channel (Prompt text + sentences, chat text + sentences, owner_words + sentences), against "Words are stored once". The brief says "change one only with a logged reason", so log both changes with a link to the source.

Sessions.say skips nothing. `Servex/agents/Sessions.js` (the new `this.write(s, Ask.refined(...))` after the chat line) calls `Ask.refined` without `Ask.skip`. A slash command or a harness-shaped turn typed into V1 or the phone sheet still becomes a refined line, and with it an open task. The hook and RemoteMCP both check the skip; this path should too.

"ONE node writer that every channel calls; no channel hand-writes the line" is only half met. `Ask.write` is used by the hook alone. Sessions.say (`this.write`), RemoteMCP.record (`fs.appendFileSync`) and Echo.process (`this.page_set(..., {refined:{…}})`, assembled by hand) each write the line themselves. RemoteMCP and Sessions at least use `Ask.refined`; Echo builds its own object. Route all four through one Ask method, so that skip, redaction and shape live in one place.

`turn_id` exists twice: `Session.turn_id` (core/Session/Session.js) and `Ask.turn_id` (Server/Ask.mjs) are copies of the same hash, and a test checks that they agree. Ask.mjs already imports from `public/` (ext/Refine/engine.js), so it can call `Session.turn_id` and the copy can go (law 6).

The tests do not cover every channel, which the brief asks for ("per channel writer… one ask line and one open task… and the readers still draw it"). Sessions.say (SDK, V1, phone sheet) and Echo have no test. Ask.test imitates the hook's call rather than running prompt-relay.mjs. No test opens a reader (chat v2/v3, the session page, PromptAudit) to show that a `tasks` Prompt still draws. plan.md says the Sessions*.test family cannot load the SDK in a worktree, so name the exact command to run after the merge in the task log, as an open step.

A turn closed with no_action still counts as open. The minion's own log says no_action scores 1 but `tally().open` still counts the Prompt. Ask.test.mjs:207 checks only `prompts.unresolved` and the score, so it passes over this. The brief requires the ask to count in `tally()` "until an agent closes it… or marks it no-action". `tally()` belongs to another agent, so this needs a filed task or a waiting entry on the parent session, not just a log line.

The diff includes `public/framework/ai/indexing-past-work.md` as a new file, but that file already exists on compliance/dev (commit d1b75f35b). Check that the merge does not overwrite the newer version. Its section 2 table (the owner's words by channel) is the only part this task should change.

Ask.test.mjs writes its scratch session into the real `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/22/.ask-test-<pid>/` and deletes it in `finally`. If the test is killed partway, that folder stays behind, and the dev server's watcher sees it in the meantime. An os.tmpdir() root would be safer, if page_tools can take one.

Sessions.say passes `now_ms()` as the refined line's `at`, while the hook and RemoteMCP pass an ISO string. Check that `now_ms()` returns the same format as `line.at`, or the two time fields on one channel will differ.
In the `refine_turn` body, the line `const text = texts.join(" ");` is indented one level short.
